This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.8,00,000/ on account of injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner had spent Rs.100,000/
towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment.

4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy,
aged about 29 years, doing business earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
And he used to spend the said amount, for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work, due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending Vehicle bearing No.KA14 R4835.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Sravanabelagola Police as per Crime No216/2018.

6. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court, and remained absent, placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
7. In the objection of the respondent No.1 has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
It is the contention of the respondent that, the accident had occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and not on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA 14R4835.
Further, contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

15. Onus probandi is on the petitioner to prove the above issue, on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
To discharge the burden lies on the petitioner - Puneethkumar relied on his affidavit evidence on 19.7.2022.
Subsequently, inspite of giving generous opportunities from 29.7.2022 to 26.9.2022, the PW1 has not come forward to lead further chief evidence.
Hence, further chief evidence of PW1 was taken as nil on 26.9.2022.
Thereafter also, inspite of giving sufficient opportunities, not present to face cross examination nor adduced further evidence.

Hence,
crossexamination of PW1 and further evidence of petitioner's side were taken as Nil on 9.11.2022 and 15.12.2022 respectively.
When the matter was posted for respondent's side evidence, the respondent No.1 has not made an effort to adduce rebuttal evidence.
Hence, the matter was posted for the stage of arguments.

16. As per law, evidence means and includes Shri Punit Kumar vs Jagadhish H on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148194619/
7 the stages of examinationinchief evidence, cross examination and reexamination.

sentences.text: The petitioner herein, in connection with the above issue, mere filing of affidavit evidence not made an effort to produce the documentary evidence in support of the stand that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA41R4835, accident in question was taken place.

Though the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner are not disputed point in issue, on going through the pleadings of the parties, the petitioner herein, has utterly failed to prove the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, by placing cogent and reliable documentary evidence for consideration.

As per law, when the witness failed to face cross examination, his mere examinationinchief evidence will not get evidentiary value to consider it, as  11 SCCH-18 MVC 3731/2019 substantive piece of evidence, as contemplated under section 137 of the Indian Evidence Act.
17 . On the other hand, no doubt, the respondent company not placed any rebuttal evidence.
But, on going through the above issue and as per section 101 of Indian Evidence Act, the petitioner has to prove the aforesaid issue.

Accordingly, I am of the view that, the petitioner herein, utterly failed to prove the above issue to the effect that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, accident in question had taken place and in the said accident,
he sustained injuries.
Hence, I am of answering the above issue in the Negative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
 18.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of relief claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition claiming compensation of Rs.8,00,000/ on account of the  12 SCCH-18 MVC 3731/2019 injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

19 . In the light of my detailed discussions on issue No.1, the petitioner herein, has failed to place convincing evidence to show that, consequent upon the accidental injuries due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner to prove the injuries sustained by him, not produced wound certificate and not made an effort to mark the other relevant documents for consideration.

And also in order to consider the compensation under different heads,
the petitioner herein, primarily not placed any police Shri Punit Kumar vs Jagadhish H on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148194619/
9 documents, wound certificate, medical documents,
age proof document, income and avocation proof documents and also not produced the evidence of doctor in order to know the nature of the injuries sustained by him and its consequences and also to know the nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner.

Apart from all these, the petitioner has  13 SCCH-18 MVC 3731/2019 not made an effort to produce police intimation and also MLC extract in order to prove the direct nexus between the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the case on hand.
In the absence of all these material documents, the petitioner will not get any compensation under different heads as sought for by the petitioner in the case on hand.

20. As per law, it is the duty of the petitioner to produce convincing documents and evidence to get the relief sought for in the case on hand, though under beneficial legislation, petition has been filed.
Hence, failure on the part of the petitioner will not gives an access to get the relief sought for by the petitioner in the case on hand.
Consequently, I am answering the issue No.2 also in the Negative.

ISSUE NO.3:
 21. In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;

10  14 SCCH-18 MVC 3731/2019  O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, no order as to costs.
Draw award accordingly.
